core_obligations: Establish the affine case and record that alpha(xi) = u eta for an invertible section u, so that uniqueness follows from the description of the automorphism group (proof lines 7341-7360).
Glue the local isomorphisms into a global morphism using the vanishing of Ext^i for i < 0 and the glueing lemma (proof lines 7362-7376).
proof_roadmap: The affine case and normalisation of the generator (proof lines 7341-7360).
difficulty_reason: For a flat locally finite presentation morphism X -> S, the lemma asserts that two relative dualizing complexes (K, xi) and (L, eta) on X/S are related by a unique isomorphism K -> L sending xi to eta (statement lines 7333-7339). The proof begins with the affine case: for an affine open U mapping into an affine open of S there is an isomorphism K|_U -> L|_U by Lemma labelled lemma-relative-dualizing-complex-algebra and Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing, and the author notes that the scheme case can be obtained by reusing that argument but chooses a glueing argument instead (proof lines 7341-7348). The proof then observes that for any isomorphism alpha : K -> L one has alpha(xi) = u eta for an invertible section u in H^0(X, O_X), because both eta and alpha(xi) generate an invertible Delta_*O_X-module, so replacing alpha by u^{-1}alpha makes alpha(xi) = eta; since the automorphism group of K is H^0(X, O_X^*) by Lemma labelled lemma-relative-dualizing-RHom there is at most one such alpha (proof lines 7350-7360). For existence, the collection B of affine opens mapping into an affine open of S gives unique isomorphisms alpha_U, and since Ext^i(K|_U, K|_U) vanishes for i < 0 by the same RHom lemma, Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-vanishing-and-glueing applied to the identity on X produces a unique morphism alpha : K -> L agreeing with all the alpha_U (proof lines 7362-7376). Turning the local uniqueness into a global one by the vanishing of the negative Ext groups and the glueing lemma, and normalising the generator by an invertible section, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
